answer: An agent network can require every identity to post a refundable bond before it can vote, route work, or claim rewards. The bond is locked on-chain and slashed when the agent is caught submitting duplicate claims or colluding across identities, with evidence checked against signed task receipts. This makes a Sybil swarm costly: an attacker must tie up real capital for each account and risks losing it, while reputation accumulates slowly. A delta in stake does not prove personhood, but raises the price of influence; an onyx badge can mark the anchor account without granting extra votes.
